extracted.intended_audience: IP litigation attorneys, corporate counsel, law firm practice managers, and analysts interpreting patent litigation cost data
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting framework for collecting and presenting estimated litigation costs for patent and other IP disputes (by case phase, risk-at-issue tiers, post-grant stages, and technology). Intended to standardize survey responses and allow temporal comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Total cost'
rubrics_metrics.description: “Total cost” was requested, and includes outside legal and paralegal services, local counsel, associates, paralegals, travel and living expenses, fees and costs for court reporters, photocopies, courier services, exhibit preparation, analytical testing, expert witnesses, translators, surveys, jury advisors, and similar expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents were to include all of the listed components (and similar expenses) in their estimate of total cost rather than only attorney fees or selected categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent eligibility / scope of estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey participants were asked to provide cost estimates, but only for the types of litigation they had personal knowledge of, either as a service provider (attorney in private practice) or as a purchaser (corporate counsel), and were engaged in relatively recently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates should be limited to matters the respondent knows firsthand and to matters with recent engagement; estimates should be for a single IP asset (i.e., one patent at issue, one trademark, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate basis: single IP asset
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were also asked to estimate based on a single IP asset (i.e., one patent at issue, one trademark, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting costs, use the scale and scope of one discrete IP asset to keep responses comparable across respondents and case types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation phase/variety breakdown (standard cost slices)
rubrics_metrics.description: For litigation (e.g., Patent Infringement, All Varieties) costs are reported by the following varieties: Initial case management; Inclusive of discovery, motions, and claim construction; Inclusive of pretrial, trial, post-trial, and appeal (when applicable); Cost of mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report costs separately for each of these discrete phases/varieties to enable stage-by-stage comparison; these are the primary slices used in the AIPLA tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-at-issue tiers for cost reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost reporting is segmented by monetary exposure tiers: Less than $1 million at risk; $1–$10 million at risk; $10–$25 million at risk; More than $25 million at risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should classify the matter by the appropriate risk tier so medians/means can be computed segment-wise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant proceedings stage breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-Grant (formerly Inter Partes) proceedings and related reviews are reported by stage: Through filing petition; Through end of motion practice; Through PTAB hearing; Through appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting post-grant costs (IPR, CBM, PGR), provide costs by these stages to show how expenses accrue through the proceeding lifecycle; new (2019) categories are reported in same stage-sliced manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered Business Method (CBM) and technology-specific PGR/IPR reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for CBM review and PGR/IPR are reported by the same stages (through filing petition, through end of motion practice, through PTAB hearing, through appeal). PGR/IPR is further stratified by technology for 2019 reporting (e.g., PGR/IPR – Electrical/Computer; PGR/IPR – Mechanical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out post-grant cost figures both by stage and (where applicable) by technology category to reflect differences in practice and complexity across technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of median, mean, and quartiles in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The report presents median litigation costs (and in charts shows 1st quartile / 3rd quartile and mean) for the various categories and stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Median is the primary central tendency metric presented in the tables; quartiles and mean are shown in charts to illustrate spread and skewness. Use these statistics when summarizing cost distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal-comparison matching guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to facilitate temporal comparisons of litigation costs to previous surveys, new varieties were matched up (when possible starting in 2017) with old varieties based mainly on the variety name. For example, Inclusive of discovery, motions, and claim construction was matched up with End of discovery, and Cost of mediation was matched up with Mediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons to historical data are approximate due to differences in variety names and definitions; exercise caution when making temporal comparisons and note possible mismatches in category definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting cost comparison metric: filing vs defending post-grant petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents were asked to compare total cost of filing a petition for post-grant proceedings (IPR, CBM or PGR) to the total cost of defending such an action; just over seven in 10 respondents (70.4%) say the total cost of filing a petition is about the same as the total cost of defending. The average cost of filing is 101.3% of the cost of defending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparative percent metrics (e.g., average cost of filing as a percent of defending) to summarize relative costs between roles (petitioner vs. defender) for post-grant matters.
